title: Header Versioning
description: Implement API versioning using custom headers like API-Version or X-API-Version, including caching, routing, and client compatibility.

data.text: Header versioning keeps a single URL per resource and negotiates the version via request headers. This is cleaner for URL space but less visible in logs. It works well when clients are controlled SDKs rather than public HTTP consumers.

rows: Custom header; simple integer or semver

data.title: Header-based versioning in Express.js
data.content: Extract the version from the header and route to the appropriate handler.

data.text: CDNs and reverse proxies cache by URL by default. If the same URL returns different representations based on headers, you must configure the Vary header correctly.

items: Always set Vary: API-Version on responses that differ by version
Set Vary: Accept for content-negotiated responses
Do not use Cache-Control: public without Vary; proxies will serve the wrong version
Test with a cache proxy (Varnish, Envoy) to verify behavior

data.title: Correct cache headers for versioned responses
data.content: The Vary header tells caches that API-Version changes the response body.
data.code:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
Cache-Control: public, max-age=60
Vary: API-Version, Accept

Body (v2):
{
  "id": "123",
  "displayName": "Alice",
  "avatarUrl": "https://cdn.example.com/avatar.png"
}

cards.title: Header Versioning
cards.description: Version via Accept or a custom API-Version header.

data.title: Visibility is a feature
data.text: URL versioning is preferred for public APIs where third-party developers need to see which version they are calling. Header versioning is better for internal APIs with controlled SDK clients.

items.question: Can I use both URL and header versioning?
items.answer: Yes, but avoid it. Pick one strategy and apply it consistently. Mixing versions in URL and header creates confusion in documentation and SDK generation.

items.question: What if a client sends an unsupported version?
items.answer: Return 400 Bad Request with a clear error message listing supported versions. Do not silently fall back to v1.

items.question: Does header versioning work with OpenAPI?
items.answer: Yes. Define a parameter with in: header and name: API-Version. Document the schema in your OpenAPI spec and generate client SDKs that include the header automatically.

data.title: Key takeaway
points: Header versioning keeps URLs clean but requires strict Vary discipline.
Use for internal APIs with controlled SDK clients.
Always document the header in OpenAPI specs.
Public APIs should prefer URL versioning for discoverability.
data.takeaway: Choose the versioning strategy that matches your audience. Public APIs need visible URLs; internal APIs can negotiate silently in headers.
